questions.question:
Let $G(V, E)$ be a simple, undirected graph. A vertex cover of $G$ is a subset $V^{\prime} \subseteq V$ such that for every $(u, v) \in E, u \in V^{\prime}$ or $v \in V^{\prime}$. Let the size of the smallest vertex cover in $G$ be $k$. Let $S$ be any vertex cover of size $k$.

For a vertex $v \in V$, which of the following constraints will always ensure that $v \in S$ ?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:

Which one of the following options gives the lowest possible value for the Jaccard coefficient between any two spanning trees of $K_{n}$ ?

questions.question: Let $R$ and $S$ be any two equivalence relations on a non-empty set $A$. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Let $R$ and $S$ be any two equivalence relations on a non-empty set $A$. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

  1. $R$ $∪$ $S$, $R$ $∩$ $S$ are both equivalence relations
  2. $R$ $∪$ $S$ is an equivalence relation
  3. $R$ $∩$ $S$ is an equivalence relation
  4. Neither $R$ $∪$ $S$ nor $R$ $∩$ $S$ are equivalence relations

$\qquad\text{“Not every graph is connected"}$

questions.title: GATE CSE 2013 | Question: 26
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.question: The line graph $L(G)$ of a simple graph $G$ is defined as follows:
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
The line graph $L(G)$ of a simple graph $G$ is defined as follows:

  • There is exactly one vertex $v(e)$ in $L(G)$ for each edge $e$ in $G$.
  • For any two edges $e$ and $e'$ in $G$, $L(G)$ has an edge between $v(e)$ and $v(e')$, if and only if $e$ and $e'$ are incident with the same vertex in $G$.

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

  • (P) The line graph of a cycle is a cycle.
  • (Q) The line graph of a clique is a clique.
  • (R) The line graph of a planar graph is planar.
  • (S) The line graph of a tree is a tree.
     
  1. $P$ only
  2. $P$ and $R$ only
  3. $R$ only
  4. $P, Q$ and $S$ only

  • All members of $B$ appear in the permutation before any of the members of $A$.

How many permutations of $U$ separate $A$ from $B?$
